Class.name: %SYS.Python
Class.Description: Provides utilities for loading and using Python modules, running Python commands, and starting the Python shell. For information on working with Python within IRIS, see Using Embedded Python.

Method.name: Import
Method.Description: Loads a Python module and returns a handle to that module. On failure, this method returns 0. Typically you use this method to bind the module to a variable, which you then use to call code within the module. For example: <example> set mypython = ##class(%SYS.Python).Import("package.subpackage.name") write mypython.helloWorld() </example>

Method.name: ActivateVenvDetail
Method.Description: Activates a Venv for only this process. Cannot be called after python has already been loaded by this process. Requires the absolute path to the given venv. </example>

Method.name: GetVenvPath
Method.Description: Returns the path for a given virtual environment tag Returns an empty string if there is no associated venv
Method.Implementation: $$$AddDBIRISSYSRoleTemporary New $namespace Set $namespace = "%SYS" if tag < 0 { Return "" } Return $GET($$$PythonVenvSyspath(tag),"")

Method.name: GetVenvTag
Method.Description: Returns the tag for a given virtual environment path Returns 0 if there is no associated venv

Method.name: PurgeVenvs
Method.Description: Delete the specified Venv from the venv global table. If no argument is provided, delete all the Venvs. Doesn't delete the CPF venv if defined, to avoid discrepencies between CPF settings and global table. </example>

Method.name: ActivateVenv
Method.Description: Activates a Venv for only this process. Cannot be called after python has already been loaded by this process. Requires the absolute path to the given venv. If possible, adds the Venv info to the prompt. Returns $$$OK or throws an error. </example>

Method.name: ValidateVenv
Method.Description: Check that a given venv can be used. Check that it exists, and that permissions are right.

Method.name: RegisterVenv
Method.Description: Looks up the definition for a Venv given a path to that Venv. Does not load python. Returns $$$OK or throws an error. </example>

Method.name: %DispatchGetProperty
Method.Description: Get a python object attribute.

Method.name: %DispatchSetProperty
Method.Description: Get a python object attribute.

Method.name: Run
Method.Description: Runs one or more Python commands; to run multiple commands, separate the commands with a new line, $char(10). This method returns 0 on success or -1 on failure.

Method.name: Path
Method.Description: Get current run time setting for PythonPath, if a new value is specified it overwrites the run time value (used by config mgr).

Method.name: ConfigureAutoML
Method.Description: An API that affects just the current process. The specified string argument will be added to sys.path relative to the instance dir on the next load of embedded python. Without args, returns the current string. With a string argument, this also loads OS Default libpython after it sets sys.path. This API is used in IML classes with "lib/automl" to reflect where the numpy is in ML enabled kits. Blocks IML from working if a non default python is already in the process (Also see AllowAutoML() ).

Method.name: AllowAutoML
Method.Description: Set an integer in system memory. Without args, return the current integer. If the integer is 1, AutoML ( ConfigureAutoML() ) will be allowed to start trying to run a non default python like the one in the CPF, for example. This is quite likely to result in AutoML errors unless what you are doing has been integrated by Intersystems.

Method.name: IRISInsidePython
Method.Description: FT counter of irispython activations

Method.name: PythonInsideIRIS
Method.Description: FT counter of libpython.so/.dll activations

Method.name: IrisPlatform
Method.Description: Returns platform (kit) identifier used in creation of IRIS kits and also in EP iris_site.py

Method.name: GetPythonInfo
Method.Description: Returns descriptive general information about process and system wide python and python related CPF settings. Informational names/API compatibility not guaranteed.
Method.Implementation: k info s info("RunningLibrary")=..GetRunningLibrary() s info("RunningVersion")=..GetPythonVersion() s info("BuildVersion")=..GetCompileTimeVersionFull() s info("BuildVersionShort")=..GetCompileTimeVersion() s cpfpp = $DATA(^|"%SYS"|CONFIG("config","PythonPath")) s cpfprl = $DATA(^|"%SYS"|CONFIG("config","PythonRuntimeLibrary")) s cpfprlv = $DATA(^|"%SYS"|CONFIG("config","PythonRuntimeLibraryVersion")) s info("CPF_PythonPath")=$case(cpfpp,0:"Not Set in CPF",:^|"%SYS"|CONFIG("config","PythonPath")) s info("CPF_PythonRuntimeLibrary")=$case(cpfprl,0:"Not Set in CPF",:^|"%SYS"|CONFIG("config","PythonRuntimeLibrary")) s info("CPF_PythonRuntimeLibraryVersion")=$case(cpfprlv,0:"Not Set in CPF",:^|"%SYS"|CONFIG("config","PythonRuntimeLibraryVersion")) s info("AllowAnyPythonForIntegratedML")=..AllowAutoML() s info("iris_site.py_platform")=..IrisPlatform() s info("PythonInsideIRIS")=..PythonInsideIRIS() s info("IRISInsidePython")=..IRISInsidePython() q

Method.name: GetPythonVersion
Method.Description: Returns descriptive version information about the python currently loaded in the process. Example: "3.10.12 (main, Jun 11 2023, 05:26:28) [GCC 11.4.0]" on Ubuntu 22. If python is not loaded it will return "Not Loaded". Does not Load Python.

Method.name: GetCompileTimeVersion
Method.Description: Returns short form python version present on the build machine used to compile IRIS

Method.name: GetCompileTimeVersionFull
Method.Description: Returns full form python version present on the build machine used to compile IRIS

Method.name: GetCompileTimePath
Method.Description: Returns python runtime library path on the build machine used to compile IRIS

Method.name: PythonRuntimeLibraryVersion
Method.Description:
Version of Python used by PythonRuntimeLibrary in Major.Minor format: 3.9, 3.11, etc.
Used in properly loading PythonRuntimeLibrary into IRIS.

Method.name: PythonRuntimeLibrary
Method.Description:
The full path (including library name) of the alternate python that you want IRIS to use in %SYS.Python.Shell() and [Language=python] for all new processes.
For example, if you install the optional python 3.11 on Ubuntu 20.04 use:
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpython3.11.so.1.0
If you install the optional python 3.8 on RH 7.9 use:
/opt/rh/rh-python38/root/usr/lib64/libpython3.8.so
If you do not use a setting here, you'll get the default OS vendor system python.

Method.name: GetRunningLibrary
Method.Description: After libpython has been loaded, by whatever means, this returns the actual libpython in use by this process.

Method.name: PerProcessRuntimeLibrarySet
Method.Description: Use this to specify what libpython you want to be loaded for just this process by a future PerProcessRuntimeLibraryStart("UserPerProcess") call. Without arguments, it returns the value that you previously set.

Method.name: PerProcessRuntimeLibraryStart
Method.Description:
Loads libpython into the current process
"UserPerProcess" will load the libpython you specified with PerProcessLibpythonSet()
"UserSystemWide" will load the libpython you specified with PythonRuntimeLibrary()
"CPF" will load the libpython you specified in the CPF
"OSDefault" will load the default libpython of the OS vendor that was compiled into IRIS
Any other argument acts as "OSDefault"
Without args it returns current flag (a number)

Method.name: PerProcessRuntimeLibrarySetPathElement
Method.Description: Set a string in process memory. Without args, return the current string. When libpython loads in the future, the specified string will be added to sys.path.

Method.name: PerProcessRuntimeLibrarySetRelativePathElement
Method.Description: Set a string in process memory. Without args, return the current string. When libpython loads in the future, the specified string will be added to sys.path relative to the instance dir.

Method.name: Bytes
Method.Description: Given an ObjectScript string, returns a Python object of type bytes. The input string cannot contain any wide character.

Method.name: CallInInit
Method.Description: An internal methods, finish "callin" initialization

Method.name: None
Method.Description: Returns the Python None value.

Method.name: True
Method.Description: Returns the Python True value.

Method.name: False
Method.Description: Returns the Python False value.

Method.name: Validate
Method.Description: Validate the internal state session, returns the number of active python objs. return -<num> if python is not inited or an invalid object is found.

Method.name: ChangeSignalState
Method.Description: Set the signal handling state 0 - swap, 1 - disable swapping iris will notify, to python signal handling

Method.name: Debugging
Method.Description: If passed true, it doesn't reset the error context before invoking any python feature (enable this before invoking any pdb method).

Method.name: Builtins
Method.Description: Loads the Python builtins module and returns a handle to that module. On failure, this method returns 0. Using this method is equivalent to using Import to load the Python builtins module.

Method.name: SetStdIOMode
Method.Description: if flags bit 1 is set, the stderr (fd 2) output will be redirected to stdout (fd 1) if there is a current COS primary device, otherwise it will behave the original way and log it in messages.log

Method.name: Install
Method.Description: This is deprecated. Please use the pip3 command line to install packages.
Method.Implementation: Write ! Write "DEPRECATED: Please use the pip3 command line to install Python packages",! Write " pip3 install ",$S(dir'="":"--target="_dir_" ",1:""),packages,! Write ! Quit $$$ERROR($$$NotImplemented)

Method.name: Shell
Method.Description:
Starts the interactive Python shell. To use this method, you must have USE permission on the %Developer resource. To exit the shell, type the command quit()

If vars is 1, then any OREF variables present in the ObjectScript shell are also available in the Python shell; the reverse is not true.

Method.name: SetInteractiveMode
Method.Description: Set the mode of python to Interactive meaning that signal handling state swaps will be allowed. Interactive mode has a performance cost, but enables useful features like saving/restoring terminal state and generating better documentation. Returns previous signal state: 0 - swapping allowed, 1 - swapping disabled, -1 - Swapping unapplicable to your platform.

Method.name: ToListTyped
Method.Description:
Given two ObjectScript lists, returns a Python list that contains the same data as contentList, with each member of the list having the data type specified in typeList. For example, the following code returns a Python list where each member of the list has the value 42, but is represented as ODBCTYPEbit(SQLBIT), ODBCTYPEnumeric(SQLNUMERIC), ODBCTYPEdecimal(SQLDECIMAL), and ODBCTYPEinteger(SQLINTEGER), respectively. More info on the type values can be found in %occODBC.inc as well as:
the docs

Include %occODBC set clist = $lb(42, 42, 42, 42) set tlist = $lb(-7, 2, 3, 4) [or] set tlist = $lb($$$ODBCTYPEbit,$$$ODBCTYPEnumeric,$$$ODBCTYPEdecimal,$$$ODBCTYPEinteger) set plist = ##class(%SYS.Python).ToListTyped(clist, tlist)
This type translation obeys Intersystems SQL Rules, so for the string and binary ODBC types, $C(0) will turn into Python "". For all ODBC types, $lb(,"") will be 2 Python "None" elements.

Method.name: To2DListTyped
Method.Description:
Takes in a 2D ObjectScript $LIST, and another $LIST with type info for each column in the first $LIST.
Returns a copy of the first $LIST as a python list with matching python types.

The types are the same as for ToListTyped.
set plist = $system.Python.To2DListTyped($lb($lb("philip",21,"electrician"),$lb("mary",22,"plumber")), $lb(12,4,12))

Method.name: ToList
Method.Description:
Given contentList (an ObjectScript list), this method returns a Python list that contains the same data. For example: set clist = $lb(123, 456.789, "hello world") set plist = ##class(%SYS.Python).ToList(clist)
Warning:
Don't pass binary data via this API, Use ToListTyped with one of the binary ODBC types instead.
If you put binary data in this API, IRIS will try to translate it as a UTF8 string.
